data.name: Leonhard
data.gender_notes: Leonhard is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Germanic name Leodegar, León or Leonardo in Latin, and Leon in Greek, meaning lion. A name of courage and strength, reminiscent of the powerful symbolism of the lion. The name Leonhard carries the meaning “Lion-hearted” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Leonhard usually hope their child will grow to embody lion-hearted and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Carries the symbolic power and courage of the lion, inspiring strength and bravery.
data.etymology: Leonhard belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lion-hearted.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Leonhard total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_english.name: Leonhard
in_english.meaning: Strong lion or brave as a lion
in_english.long_meaning: The name Leonhard is derived from the Old High German words 'leō' meaning lion and 'hart' meaning brave or strong, thus it translates to strong lion or brave as a lion. This name symbolizes courage, strength, and bravery, reflecting the characteristics of a lion, known as the king of the jungle. Historically, the name Leonhard has been associated with Saint Leonhard, a 6th-century bishop known for his piety and kindness. The name has been popularized across Europe and is still used today in various cultures, embodying the spiritual significance of courage and resilience.

data.cultural_impact: Throughout history, the name Leonhard has been popular in various cultures and regions, most notably in Europe. In Germanic traditions, names ending in 'hard' symbolize strength, bravery, and power-traits associated with the character of a proud and noble warrior-the lion. This name has been borne by numerous kings, dukes, and nobles, including St. Leonhard, a 6th-century saint, who holds significant patronage over farmers, travelers, and animals, particularly horses. Leonhard's Day, celebrated on November 17, is an important feast day in some European countries like Austria, Bavaria, Galicia, and Nordic countries.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian spirituality, the name Leonhard conveys qualities of a brave and steadfast soul. The lion, a powerful symbol of courage and Christ's assertiveness, embodies the unwavering faith and dedication one might embody while following the path to God. As a Saint, Leonhard (either Leodegar or Leo) came to be revered as a protector, offering comfort, strength, and guidance to those in need. In folklore, Leonhard is often depicted as taking care of orphaned animals, providing shelter to wayfarers, and caring for those who care for animals. Thus, the name Leonhard stands as a reminder of the divine strength and courage that we have within ourselves to overcome the challenges and struggles in our lives and remain steadfast on our spiritual journey.
